text_blocks.snippet: Common scams targeting residents across Central Illinois include fraudulent text messages about fake traffic or toll violations, imposter phone calls from government agencies, and online purchase or delivery issues.
Fake Toll and Traffic Violation Texts

list.snippet: Scammers send text messages claiming you owe money for unpaid tolls or traffic tickets, threatening suspension of your driver's license.

The text often includes a malicious link to steal your credit card or personal data

.
Note: State agencies like the Illinois Secretary of State or IDOT do not text people unprompted requests for fine payments.
Fraudsters text claiming a delivery (via USPS, UPS, or generic carriers) is delayed or missing a house number.

They ask you to click a link to pay a small redelivery fee or verify your address, which compromises your financial details
.
Callers or texters pose as the FCC, police, or local courts, claiming your phone number or identity is tied to a crime.

They use urgency and fear to demand immediate payment or sensitive personal information
.
Con artists list fake goods or non-existent companion pets on social media yard sale pages or online classifieds.

They ask for non-traditional or hard-to-reverse payments (wire transfers, cash apps, or gift cards) and invent extra fee complications
.
Never click unexpected links in text messages or emails regarding fines or package deliveries.

Verify independently
by looking up the official phone number of the agency or business rather than calling the number in the text.

Report fraud using local or federal resources like the [Better Business Bureau of Central Illinois](bbb.org bureau-of-central-illinois-inc-0724-380120155) or file a complaint with the Illinois Attorney General
.

text_blocks.snippet: If you or someone you know was targeted, let me know how they were contacted (text, phone call, or email) and what the message claimed, and I can help you figure out if it is a known scam.
